lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: What are you crying for, Tantalus? Why are you standing in a lake just to mope?

lines.speaker: Tantalus
lines.text: Because, Menippus, I'm dying of thirst.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Are you that lazy? Just bend down and take a sip. Or, I don't know, cup your hands.

lines.speaker: Tantalus
lines.text: Bending down doesn't work. The water runs away the second it sees me coming. And if I do manage to scoop some up... before it can even touch my lips, it just slips right through my fingers. I don't know how it does it. Look, my hands are bone dry.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: That's a neat trick. [pause] But tell me, Tantalus—why do you actually need to drink? You don't have a body anymore. That's buried back in Lydia somewhere. Your body could get hungry and thirsty, sure. But you're a soul. How exactly does a ghost get thirsty?

lines.speaker: Tantalus
lines.text: That is the punishment. My soul gets thirsty as if it were a body.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Right, fine, I'll take your word for it—you're being punished with thirst. But what's the actual problem? Are you worried you're going to die of dehydration? Because as far as I can see, there isn't a basement under the Underworld for you to drop dead into.

lines.speaker: Tantalus
lines.text: That's true. But that's part of the sentence too—the desperate urge to drink when you don't actually need to.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: You're completely delusional, Tantalus. Though now that you mention it, you do look like you need a drink—a good stiff dose of hellebore for the madness. You've got reverse rabies. You're not afraid of the water, you're terrified of the thirst.

lines.speaker: Tantalus
lines.text: [crying] I'll drink the hellebore, Menippus! I don't care! Just let me have it!

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: [laughs] Cheer up, Tantalus. You're not getting a drink, and neither is anyone else down here. It's anatomically impossible. You're just the only one with a court-ordered puddle dodging your hands.
